chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Is there Zakat upon the wealth of the orphan?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless it is traded with or worked with.'
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat obligatory on an orphan's savings or capital?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Zakat is not levied on the preserved capital of an orphan but only when it is actively employed in trade or commerce to generate profit. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between passive wealth preservation and active commercial engagement, ensuring that the guardian's management aligns with the principles of wealth growth required for Zakat liability. The hadith underscores the protective nature of Shia fiqh regarding orphans' assets, preventing unnecessary financial burden while encouraging productive use of their wealth.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Is there Zakāt upon the wealth of the orphans?’ Heasws said: ‘No, unless if one were to trade with it, or work with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if there is Zakat on orphan’s assets. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat is not due unless it is used in business or is made to work.’”
